newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy ready to help maintain Albania peace - Dini.
newsitem.headline: Italy ready to help maintain Albania peace - Dini.

text.p: Italy would be ready to send troops to Albania to help maintain order once a new, broad-based government has been set up, Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini was quoted as saying on Wednesday.
Dini told La Repubblica newspaper that European governments have asked Albanian President Sali Berisha to form a cross-party administration and hold a fresh general election within 45 days.

"(The Italian government) is ready to send financial and technical aid to help an economic recovery and even soldiers -- a contingent to reinforce the Albanian forces and prevent organised crime taking advantage of the chaos and increasing the flow of illegal immigrants to Italy," Dini said.
"But to do all this we must have an Albanian government we can talk to," he added.

The Albanian government of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi and his ministers resigned on Saturday after an explosion of violence in the south of the country sparked by smouldering discontent over the collapse of popular investment schemes.
Parliament has since declared a state of emergency and has issued orders for the army to shoot armed rioters on sight.
Berisha has accused opposition parties of resorting to violence to try to seize power, but Dini said the "revolt" was not political. "This is a spontaneous rebellion of the people."

He said Berisha, who was elected to a new five-year term on Monday by parliament, had assured Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi earlier this week that he would accept European demands for swift new elections.
"But I have to be sceptical," Dini said, adding that the Italian government had heard nothing from Berisha over the past 48-hours. "This silence...worries us," he said.
Dini also hinted at strains within the 15-nation European Union over the handling of the situation.
"We cannot hide the fact that within the EU, Nordic countries are keeping their distance from events in the Balkans," Dini said. "Agreements aren't the easiest thing."
He also said that Italy had not received the assurances it had looked for from opposition forces in Albania over their willingness to work with Berisha.

Italy, which briefly occupied Albania during World War Two, lies a short distance across the Adriatic from the Balkan country. It has seen an influx of illegal Albanian immigrants since the collapse of Stalinist rule and has put coastguards on alert for a possible fresh exodus following the weekend unrest.
